judged_text: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]', so minimumTokenResponseSchema is a plain object schema whose only real field is access_token, and Zod's default strip mode drops every other property of the token response. When credential sharing is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse validates nothing but access_token and silently strips the fields callers persist: Salesforce's stored credential loses instance_url/id/scope (breaking the jsforce connection after the credential is reloaded), and for credentials with a null userId (team credentials) the real provider response is loose-parsed, overwriting the stored refresh_token with the literal placeholder 'refresh_token' and permanently destroying the user's refresh token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, but `z.string()` is a Zod object whose `.toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"`. This means the schema does not actually allow arbitrary expiry fields (e.g., `expiry_date`, `expires_in`) and, because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, `safeParse` will drop all provider fields other than `access_token` (and the unusable `"[object Object]"` key). When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, callers that persist `tokenResponse.data` will lose important fields (e.g., Salesforce will lose `instance_url`, `id`, `scope`, etc. in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`). Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the literal placeholder `"refresh_token"` when missing, which can overwrite an existing stored refresh token in flows that merge parsed data back into existing credentials (e.g., Office365 merges `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)`), and the function’s condition does not exclude team credentials (it ignores `userId`), so the overwrite can apply even when the refresh was not actually performed via the sync endpoint.
